notices.hold_reason: The notice is printed as '. . . (date of transaction) “You may cancel this transaction ... ”': the date line sits outside the opening quotation mark and the sentence says 'from the above date'. Cutting inside the quotes leaves the notice without its date line; cutting from the date line would print an unbalanced quotation mark. Held rather than print a notice that points to a date line it does not have.

unsure: RI-cancel: the 6-28-4 block is a whole section with a deposit refund rule in subsection (d) around the two notices, so it is held rather than printed.

RI-62: the age that makes a person elderly is in 42-66-4.1, which the file did not fetch, and the builder does not know buyer age, so this would be on_file at best; it is held because the block is the whole 5-65-27 section.
RI-lien: both copies of the lien notice are inside whole statute sections with operative text, so none is loaded even though two official copies exist.

RI-board: the Board flyer (agency guidance, not law) may be the Summary of Registration Law that 5-65-3(k) says is handed to the owner when work begins, but the file only quotes its insurance paragraph, so it is not loaded.
RI-lien-statement: added because 5-65-18 puts a lien statement in every written contract, but the statute prescribes no sentence.

RI-lien: printed on every contract (applies {}), because 34-28-4.1 says a contractor dealing directly with the owner cannot claim a lien without giving the notice; 5-65-3(o) ties the written-contract duty to work over $1,000.
RI-cancel-form: held because the '. . . (date of transaction)' line precedes the opening quotation mark (see hold_reason). RI-62 (stored only) has the same edge and is cut inside the quotes.
